messages:
Sophie: Heads-up — thinking about adding a tiny 'mini-bench' stage between admit and full bench to catch obvious OOM/latency regressions on new ingest candidates. Quick, cheap, and deterministic. Thoughts?
Ranjit: +1 in principle. Where does it run? dedicated small GPU pool or cpu emulation?
Sophie: Ideally a tiny GPU slice (1xA10G equiv) with fixed batch=1 sequences to surface runtime ffi/alloc regressions. CPU emulation misses many failure modes.
Mike: Cost tradeoff: if we run on GPU for every ingest candidate we'll pay a lot. Can we gate by file size + model type? e.g., only on >100M params or quantized formats we care about.
Leo: Agree on gating. Also we should keep the mini-bench deterministic: same prompt set (20 short inferences) + KV warmup. That'll reduce noise and help diffs.
Alexa: Ops question: how do we record artifacts and integrate with the admit flow? I want a canonical output bundle with profiler snapshots + logs so SRE can triage quickly.
Sophie: Proposal: mini-bench outputs a single gzipped artifact: metrics.json, perf.pb (tiny perf counters), runtime.log, and a smoke.wave binary for replay. Store in s3://intake-mini-bench/YYYY/MM/<model-id>. Add a flag `mini_bench: {enabled: true, tier: "auto"}` to the ingest manifest.
Ranjit: That storage path is fine. We should also add an opt-out annotation for private/customer builds. e.g., `mini_bench: {enabled: false, reason: "air-gapped"}`
Mike: How do we keep this from becoming another flaky test? We need SLOs: if p50 latency regresses >20% or any OOM -> fail admit. If it's within noise, pass.
Leo: Add an admission verdict enum: PASS / WARN / FAIL. WARN = regression but within rollback policy; FAIL = OOM or severe regression. Then the gate can bubble up to humans for WARNs.
Alexa: Can we reuse existing bench infra? We should avoid building a separate runner. Maybe a lightweight runner that calls the same serving runtime but with constrained resources.
Sophie: Yes reuse runtime binary but with a `--mini-bench-mode` flag that reduces concurrency and enables extra telemetry. Runner only needs to be ~200 LOC wrapper.
benchbot: deploy-bot: mini-bench runner image build succeeded for commit abc123 — pushed to quay.redwood/mini-bench:20240525
Ranjit: Good. One more interface question: where do we express the bench inputs? Keep them next to the model manifest or reference a shared corpus id?
Sophie: Let's reference shared corpus ids to keep manifests small. manifest example: ```yaml
model_id: foo-v2
mini_bench:
  enabled: auto
  corpus: rev-smoke-202405
  timeout_s: 45
```
Mike: Timeline: can we pilot for 2 weeks on a subset of new models (OSS-largest + quantized floats)? Track cost delta and number of catches.
Sophie: Sounds good. I'll draft a short RFC follow-up with the gating rules, artifact schema, and failure semantics. Meeting to sync Thursday 10am? :calendar:
Leo: I'll join. Also add a short runbook snippet for oncall to triage FAIL vs WARN.
Alexa: I'll sketch the artifact schema and upload to the RFC PR.
Sophie: Thanks — I'll open the PR with checklist and action items.
